messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: The result of Std.nox isn't posed
parts:
it does not work
summary(fit, standardized = c(“std.all”, “std.nox”))

but I find this would work:
summary(fit, standardized = c(“std.lv”, “std.nox”))

it seems that “std.all”, “std.nox” cannot exist in one result.

Weird, took a minute to track down the problem.  summary() actually does provide std.nox with std.all, but you won't see it printed by the print.lavaan.parameterEstimates() method.

PE <- summary(fit, standardized = c("std.all", "std.nox"))$pe
PE                # std.nox not printed,
PE$std.nox        # but it is there, and
as.data.frame(PE) # it is printed by the print.data.frame() method


@Yves, the issue is lines 415-419 of lav_print.R:

  # if standardized, remove std.nox column (space reasons only)
  # unless, std.all is already removed
  if (!is.null(y$std.all)) {
    y$std.nox <- NULL
  }

Ages ago, lavaan would print all 3 standardized solutions by default, which made the Console output wider than the standard acceptable 80 characters.  Omitting one of the 3 standardized solutions was a way to prevent that.  When you explicitly requested only std.all and std.nox (a feature I added last year), the above logic still removes std.nox unnecessarily.  To prevent that, I could update the print method to only remove it when std.lv and std.all are already there:

  # if 3 standardized solutions, remove std.nox column
  if (!is.null(y$std.lv) && !is.null(y$std.all)) {
    y$std.nox <- NULL
  }

But I was never in favor of printing std.lv by default (which is why I updated the standardized= argument to accept a character string).  In my opinion, when all 3 exist, it would be better to drop std.lv:

  # if 3 standardized solutions, remove std.lv column
  if (!is.null(y$std.nox) && !is.null(y$std.all)) {
    y$std.lv <- NULL
  }

@Yves, I can send a pull request if you let me know which solution you prefer.

parts:
> @Yves, I can send a pull request if you let me know which solution you
> prefer.

I am rather fond of the std.lv column!

I also think that it rarely make sense to have both std.nox and std.all.
If you have 'x' variables that you don't want to standardized, std.nox
is the way to go, and std.all is redundant.

Anyway, I would prefer the following behavior: if a user specifies
standardized = "std.nox", only the std.nox column is shown (not
std.all). If a user specifies standardized = c("std.nox", "std.all"),
then both columns are shown.

Yves.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: The result of Std.nox isn't posed
parts:
I also think that it rarely make sense to have both std.nox and std.all.
If you have 'x' variables that you don't want to standardized, std.nox
is the way to go, and std.all is redundant.

I might want both, depending on each "x" variable's scale.  Suppose there is a continuous and a binary exogenous predictor.  I would want the standardized slope of the continuous predictor (standardizing "x" too), but not for the binary predictor (only standardize the outcome, so it is a standardized (conditional) mean difference).

I would prefer the following behavior: if a user specifies
standardized = "std.nox", only the std.nox column is shown (not
std.all). If a user specifies standardized = c("std.nox", "std.all"),
then both columns are shown.

That sounds reasonable, but I have trouble seeing how this information would be passed along to the print method.  When standardized=TRUE, the default character strings are set in parameterEstimates().  The print.lavaan.parameterEstimates() method just looks for which columns are present.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: The result of Std.nox isn't posed
parts:
Maybe print.lavaan.parameterEstimates() shouldn't choose at all whether to show a subset of columns.  There are other things the user can choose that would make the summary() output "too wide" (e.g., a high nd=, or adding ci=TRUE and standardized=TRUE), which lavaan doesn't try to anticipate.

I think the solution is to just update the default output when TRUE.  When it checks for any "x" variables when fixed.x=TRUE, instead of adding "std.nox" to the list, it could replace "std.all" (and "std.lv" remains in either default).  If people want both, they can explicitly request both, and they will be printed.
